_comment: Phase 5 Stage 1 NPC dialogue (ROADMAP 'dialogue stored in JSON for easy editing'), extended by Phase 5 Stage 2 with a store-opening trigger. One entry per npc id (matching map_layouts' npcs() ids): name = the dialogue box's speaker plate, start = the node shown on interact, nodes = id -> {text, next?} for linear beats, {text, choices: [{text, next}]} for a branch point, or {text} alone for a terminal node (advancing closes the box). A choice's "next" can also be the literal sentinel string "OPEN_STORE", recognized by scripts/dialogue_ui.gd's _advance() (NOT scripts/dialogue_db.gd, which stays domain-agnostic pure traversal) — landing on it closes the dialogue box and opens scripts/store_ui.gd instead of going to another node. Only Marta's tree uses it this stage (she's the only shopkeeper), but the mechanism itself isn't Marta-specific. Loaded via scripts/dialogue_db.gd only — see its header for the traversal rules. Tone contract: GDD.md section 9 ('people who have chosen hope and are a little funny about it'); every character's dialogue is static flavor this stage — no quest hooks, affinity, or schedule reactivity until Phases 7/13. Writing note: the pixel font's glyph set has no > < [ ] $ % & * = etc. (see art/ui/README.md) — stick to letters, digits, and basic punctuation in all text below.

greet.text: Ah — the new farmer. Harlan. Mayor, more or less, since nobody else wanted the paperwork.

founding.text: Twenty-five years ago this town was a fence post and an argument. Now look at it. A whole town's worth of arguments.

offer.text: You look like you could use work, and I keep a list. Interested?

offer_yes.text: Good answer. For now, grow things — a town runs on its stomach. I'll have proper work for you soon enough.

offer_no.text: Look all you like. The fence keeps the wasteland out, not the neighbors. When you're ready to be useful, mine's the ugly house with the good roof.

greet.text: Morning! Marta. If it's worth trading, it comes through here — seeds, tools, gossip. The gossip's free.

stocktake.text: Just finished the morning count — seeds, tools, tinned rations, all present and only mildly suspicious. Credits only, mind — I don't care what the bottle-cap man says, that is not money.

chicken.text: The two-headed chicken got into the seed bins again. Both heads deny it. I've recounted twice just to be sure it didn't eat the profits.

greet.text: Hold up — new face. Kael. I scout the road east so the road east doesn't scout us.

city.text: Past this gate, half a day's walk, there's the old city. Towers taller than anything alive, streets that still remember cars.

ask.text: Everything the fence keeps out lives there. So of course everyone keeps asking me what's inside.

inside.text: Salvage. Medicine. Machines that hum if you're lucky, things that bite if you're not. When you're ready — and better armed — I'll walk you in myself.

danger.text: Smart. It is. That's why I go careful and come home every time. Home's the whole trick — lamplight at your back going out, lamplight in front coming home.

greet.text: Silas. This is the Sanctuary — what's left of it. Mind the grey goat, she bites what she can reach and she can reach further than you'd think.

stock.text: Every beast in these pens comes down from one stubborn line I kept breathing through the bad years. Pre-war stock's gone soft and precious; the mutant kind are ugly and near unkillable. Out here you keep both, or you keep neither long.

offer.text: You'll want animals of your own soon enough. Something with a pulse to put in a barn. That what walks you down here?

not_yet.text: Not yet you can't. I'll not sell a living creature to somebody with nowhere to put it — build yourself a barn or a coop first, then we'll talk feed and fair prices. Come back when you've got walls and a roof for them, and I'll set you up proper.

look.text: Look all you like — half the town wanders down just to. The one with the extra horn is Dorothy. She's meaner than the wasteland and twice as hard to kill, and she knows it.
